questions.q: What turns a market "idea" into an actual trading strategy?
options: Believing in it strongly enough to trade real money
Specifying universe, signal, sizing, risk rules, and execution unambiguously enough to run without a human in the loop
Backtesting it once and seeing a positive return
Giving it a catchy name
questions.explain: A strategy is a fully specified, rule-based mapping from data to positions. Without all five components nailed down, it's a hunch, not something that can be executed consistently or backtested honestly.

questions.q: What makes a strategy "systematic" rather than "discretionary"?
options: It only trades stocks, never other asset classes
It is always profitable
Given the same data, it always produces the same decision — no human judgment call in the moment
It uses more advanced math than a discretionary approach
questions.explain: Systematic means deterministic: the same inputs always produce the same output. Discretionary trading uses rules as input to human judgment, so the same chart can produce different decisions from different traders.

questions.q: Why does determinism matter for a trading strategy?
options: It's required by regulators
It guarantees the strategy will be profitable
It's what makes the strategy backtestable — you can replay history and get a reproducible result
It makes the strategy immune to changing market conditions
questions.explain: A backtest only means something if running the same rules against the same historical data always produces the same outcome. That reproducibility is the whole point of determinism.

questions.q: A rule says "trade the stocks that performed best last year." What's the problem with this as a universe definition?
options: There is no problem, this is a valid universe
It uses hindsight — "performed best" can only be known after the fact, so it can't be used to pick a universe in advance
It only works for stocks, not currencies
It requires too much computing power
questions.explain: A universe has to be defined using only information available at the time, not after the fact. Picking a universe based on which instruments already did well is a form of lookahead bias, covered in depth in Chapter 4.

questions.q: What is the honest, stated reality about most systematic trading ideas, according to this lesson?
options: Most ideas are profitable once properly coded
Most ideas do not survive a rigorous out-of-sample test, and that is the normal state of the field
Ideas are guaranteed to work if backtested on enough data
This course guarantees a working strategy by the end
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that most strategy ideas fail rigorous testing, and that this course teaches research discipline and engineering skill rather than a guaranteed profit formula.
